execution_context.file_location: PowerShell script delivered via malicious document or web download

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PowerShell command that downloads and executes a remote RAT payload (exact code not provided in the report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads and executes a remote PowerShell RAT payload, establishing a command-and-control channel for remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote code is a classic sign of malware, especially when delivered via social engineering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PowerShell scripts should not download and execute code from untrusted sources without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment scripts in trusted enterprise environments may download and execute code, but only from vetted sources.
key_indicators: PowerShell execution from document or web download

execution_context.file_location: PowerShell command executed post-exploitation on VMware Horizon server

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PowerShell command that installs the NukeSped backdoor (exact code not provided in the report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes a PowerShell command to install the NukeSped backdoor, enabling persistent remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Post-exploitation installation of a backdoor is a hallmark of targeted APT activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: VMware Horizon servers should not execute arbitrary PowerShell commands that install persistent malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use PowerShell for legitimate remote management, but not for installing unauthorized backdoors.

attack_chain.action: Victim is lured to a malicious website or document promising exclusive news about Ukraine.
Malicious PowerShell script is executed, downloading and running a remote RAT payload.
On compromised VMware Horizon servers, attackers exploit Log4J vulnerability to gain code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of PowerShell command to install NukeSped backdoor

attack_chain.action: PowerShell command installs NukeSped backdoor for persistent access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Long-term remote access and data exfiltration

behavioral_signatures: PowerShell execution from documents or web downloads
PowerShell scripts downloading and executing remote payloads
Installation of known backdoors (e.g., NukeSped) via PowerShell
Unusual PowerShell activity on VMware Horizon servers
file_indicators: Malicious PowerShell scripts delivered as attachments or via web downloads
Unexpected PowerShell scripts or scheduled tasks on servers
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure associated with PowerShell RATs or NukeSped
Unusual network activity from endpoints shortly after PowerShell execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PowerShell execution events, especially those triggered by documents or web downloads. Flag PowerShell scripts that download and execute remote code. On VMware Horizon servers, alert on any PowerShell activity that installs persistent binaries or backdoors. Correlate with known C2 domains and backdoor signatures.
